_comment: Machine-owned gate baseline. Read and written by
scripts/check-quality-ratchet.sh. Do NOT restate these numbers in
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md or ROADMAP.md -- prose has nothing
validating it, and the previous AGENTS.md claim of 'Credo strict: 0
issues, Dialyzer clean' was wrong by 1187 and 127 respectively.
Counts may only go down. Lower one, then run with --update.

credo.counts_lines_matching: length of the .issues array in credo's JSON document
credo.scope: lib/ src/ test/ web/ apps/ packages/ per .credo.exs
notes: Measured with --format json, NOT --format flycheck. The JSON document is
a completion marker: a crashed run yields unparseable output rather than
zero matching lines. Counting flycheck lines with `grep -c` returned 0 on
a crash, which the ratchet read as a perfect score.
Credo prints mix compile lines and an 'info: Some source files could not
be parsed correctly' notice to STDOUT before the document, so the reader
must take everything from the first bare '{'. Findings are on STDOUT
(dialyzer's are on STDERR).
SCOPE IS LOAD-BEARING: .credo.exs must list packages/. Without it this
same run reports 232 instead of 1182, because packages/ is ~58% of the
source tree. A narrowed scope makes the gate report a false improvement
and, on --update, bakes the narrower coverage in permanently.
CANNOT BE SHARDED: mix credo <path> analyzes nothing against this
config, so the repo-wide count must come from one pass.
The 2991s in runtime_seconds above is NOT the cost of the analysis.
One full --strict pass measured 95.4s of analysis in CI (73 checks,
3405 files, run 34168895863) and 161s locally including the compile,
so 2991 covers a cold umbrella compile, not the scan. This gate is
blocking per-PR on that basis; re-measure before demoting it.
DO NOT swap this gate for `credo diff`. Its issue identity is not
stable across the two revisions it compares, so it invents both
halves of a delta: on a PR touching only YAML and JSON it reported
209 new refactoring, 108 new readability and 138 new design findings
while also claiming 659 refactoring and 49 readability were fixed.
The absolute count here has no such ambiguity, and is the same number
nightly measures.

dialyzer.counts_lines_matching: Total errors minus Skipped, from dialyxir's summary line
dialyzer.scope: root app beams only; packages/ contribute zero findings
notes: 118 = Total errors (134) minus Skipped (16), i.e. the findings dialyzer
actually reports after .dialyzer_ignore.exs on the reference toolchain.
The previous 91 baseline came from a warm PLT and was not reproducible:
fresh reference-toolchain runs report 118 both locally and in PR CI, while
nightly's obsolete Elixir 1.19/OTP 27 literals reported 111. The baseline
was reset with --allow-regression only after nightly moved to mise.toml.
Do NOT baseline the raw 'Total errors:' number: it is the count BEFORE the
ignore file, so a landed suppression leaves it unchanged and is invisible.
PLT TRAP 1 -- staleness. dialyxir keys its deps PLT off the DEPS hash,
which a path dependency does not move, so editing or adding a module under
packages/ leaves the PLT describing the old code. A fix removing 16 errors
read as a no-op across two full runs. check-quality-ratchet.sh detects this
by hashing packages/*/lib content and stamping the hash next to the PLT.
Do not detect it by mtime: actions/checkout writes sources with mtime=now
while actions/cache restores the PLT with its archived mtime, so an
mtime check fires on every warm-cache CI run.
PLT TRAP 2 -- under-population. Never run `mix dialyzer --plt` to repair a
discarded deps PLT: it produces a file the size of core.plt (1.98 MB vs
11.8 MB populated) with no dependency apps, after which dialyxir reports
'PLT is up to date!' forever because freshness comes from a 20-byte
.plt.hash. Analysing against it gave 2055 findings, 1845 of them
unknown_function -- a fabricated regression. Discard the PLT and let the
analysis run rebuild it. The ratchet refuses to report a count when
unknown_function exceeds a quarter of the findings (healthy: 3 of 118).
